sources.name: Stanford Careers (careersearch.stanford.edu) - Oracle HCM Candidate Experience
sources.what_it_contains: University staff/academic requisitions (415 open reqs at fetch time). Verified by JobFamily census: Research 116, Administration 79, Finance 20, Bargaining Unit-TMS 20, Student Services 19, IT 19, ... NO student-hourly / student-assistant requisitions. 'Student Services' is a staff job family (Student Services Officer/Specialist), not student employment. Keyword searches for 'casual' returned 4 relevance-ranked staff jobs and none were student roles.

json_api.notes: Both endpoints returned HTTP 200 with plain JSON, no auth header, no cookie, no Referer needed. Standard desktop User-Agent used. siteNumber CX_1 was read out of the landing page HTML (siteFavicon links contain siteNumber=CX_1). Other siteNumber values (CX_2, CX_1001, CX_1002) also return 200 but are not the Stanford site.

sources.paging: Search endpoint: items[0].TotalJobsCount gives the total (415 at fetch time). Page with offset= in the finder string, limit=200 accepted (limit is the max page size that worked). Requisitions are in items[0].requisitionList[]. Loop offset 0,200,400... until requisitionList is empty. De-dupe on Id. Then hit the detail endpoint per Id for ExternalDescriptionStr / ExternalQualificationsStr / workLocation.
sources.public_posting_url_pattern: https://careersearch.stanford.edu/hcmUI/CandidateExperience/en/sites/stanford/job/<Id>  (verified 200). The slug form https://careersearch.stanford.edu/jobs/<slug>-<id> that appears in search-engine results 404s - do not use it.
sources.fetch_notes: Fetched 2026-08-31. Useful for part-time staff roles only; not a student-employment source.

sources.name: Handshake (Stanford Career Education) - the official student job board
sources.what_it_contains: The primary, university-designated listing service for Stanford student part-time jobs. Administrative Guide 10.1.1 section 2.a: 'Stanford departments wishing to hire undergraduate students as part-time workers are strongly encouraged to use the Handshake system administered by Stanford Career Education to list their job openings. Programs should log onto https://stanford.joinhandshake.com/login to post a job'. Financial Aid's Student Employment page likewise says 'you can apply for jobs through Stanford's new career services platform, Handshake'.
sources.paging: NOT SCRAPABLE WITHOUT AUTH. https://stanford.joinhandshake.com/stu/postings redirects (HTTP 200 after redirect) to https://stanford.joinhandshake.com/login. Requires SUNet SSO. Any scraper would need an authenticated session or the Handshake partner API; no public listing endpoint exists.
sources.fetch_notes: Verified 2026-08-31 by curl: /stu/postings -> /login. Zero postings harvestable. This is the single biggest gap - the majority of Stanford student jobs live here and are NOT publicly visible.

sources.name: Stanford Financial Aid - Student Employment
sources.what_it_contains: Policy/eligibility only - NO job listings. Explicitly states 'our office does not make job assignments'. Sub-pages: Federal Work-Study https://financialaid.stanford.edu/aid/employ/fws/index.html and Community Service Federal Work-Study https://financialaid.stanford.edu/aid/employ/csws/index.html (both HTTP 200).
sources.paging: No listings to page. Static HTML; scrape once for eligibility rules to enrich other postings (FWS eligibility, summer vs academic year).
sources.fetch_notes: IMPORTANT - dead URLs: https://financialaid.stanford.edu/undergrad/work/ and https://financialaid.stanford.edu/aid/employ/wage_scale BOTH redirect to https://financialaid.stanford.edu/errors/404page.html. The live index page footer reads 'Updated on August 31, 2022', so this content is stale. https://studentjobs.stanford.edu does not resolve at all (curl exit 000, no DNS/TLS).

sources.name: Stanford Administrative Guide, Chapter 10 - Student Employment and Assistantships
sources.what_it_contains: Authoritative policy, no listings. Guide Memo 10.1.1 (https://adminguide.stanford.edu/chapters/student-employment-and-assistantships/undergraduate-student-employment-campus-0) fetched in full: all Stanford student employment is hourly (except graduate assistantships); undergrad jobs 'should not typically require more than 15 hours per week' during an enrollment period; full-time allowed during between-quarter breaks; 'All job postings must include the pay range for the position.'
sources.paging: Static HTML, one page per memo. Scrape once; use to validate hours/pay constraints on harvested postings.

sources.name: R&DE (Residential & Dining Enterprises) Student Employment

Scrape by parsing anchors in the main-content region; roles are standing/evergreen rather than dated requisitions, so diff on role title + body text rather than on a posting id. Re-poll weekly.
sources.fetch_notes: Fetched 2026-08-31, HTTP 200. All three apply links point to the same portal https://rdeapps.stanford.edu/HRApps/.

sources.name: The Hub @ Lathrop / Learning Technologies & Spaces (Student Affairs) - Student Jobs
sources.what_it_contains: The richest fully-public student-IT source found. Four student positions, each with its own public JD page carrying explicit pay, minimum weekly hours, available terms, required qualifications, responsibilities and a team contact email.
sources.paging: Index page https://thehub.stanford.edu/jobs lists 4 roles; each links to a sibling JD page (/student-technical-consultant-job-description, /tech-desk-consultant-job-description, /informal-spaces-tech-job-description, /createspace-consultant-job-description). No pagination. Scrape the index for anchors ending in '-job-description', then fetch each; parse the 'Main content start'..'Back to Top' region, and read the mailto: for contact. All four share one apply form.
sources.fetch_notes: Fetched 2026-08-31, all 5 pages HTTP 200. This is a UIT-adjacent Student Affairs unit, not uit.stanford.edu; UIT itself has no public student-job listing page (see notes below).

sources.name: Stanford Recreation & Wellness - Employment Opportunities
sources.what_it_contains: Public listing of 14 currently-advertised part-time recreation roles grouped by unit (Campus Aquatics, Academic Programs, Intramural Sports, Fitness, Climbing Wall, Redwood City SRWC, Membership Services, Adventure Programs, Youth Programs), with a per-unit contact email and a page-level pay range of $17/hour to $25/hour.
sources.paging: Single flat HTML page, no pagination. Roles are grouped under h-tags per unit with a 'Contact information: <email>' line, and each role title is an anchor to a Google Drive/Docs JD. Apply is either a downloadable electronic application (Google Drive) or a Teamworks form (teamworksapp.com/ext/...). Re-poll seasonally - some roles are annotated seasonal.
sources.fetch_notes: Fetched 2026-08-31, HTTP 200. NOTE the correct host is rec.stanford.edu; recreation.stanford.edu and cardinalrecreation.stanford.edu do NOT resolve (curl exit 000). Individual JDs live on drive.google.com / docs.google.com and were NOT fetched in this run, so per-role pay and requirements are unknown - only the page-level $17-$25/hour range is evidenced.

sources.name: Stanford Residential Education (ResEd) - Student Internships

sources.fetch_notes: Fetched 2026-08-31, HTTP 200. Guide Memo 10.1.1 notes these residence roles carry a stipend to defray living expenses rather than hourly wages, and that stipends may affect need-based aid and athletic scholarships.

postings.description: Join the R&DE Student Connect team. In this role you help amplify student voices and share useful information about campus dining and housing while enhancing R&DE's connection to students. Projects include learning about the inner workings of R&DE and sharing tips students can use to maximize their living and dining experience; contributing design, photography and communications projects; producing videos and social media content; leading focus groups and surveys to gather feedback on student preferences and expectations; and planning community events. postings.description: The Halal Dining Intern acts as a liaison for R&DE Stanford Dining, Hospitality & Auxiliaries (SDHA) and the Muslim students it serves, to facilitate engagement in the community for those observing a Halal diet. Job purpose: to assist the R&DE SDHA team in the execution, improvement and evaluation of current programs and services relating to halal dining and Ramadan. Reports to the Director of Student Hospitality Excellence. Duties can include: maintain the R&DE Dining Menu Portal; vet CORE and event menus for ingredients and specifically foods that are in line with and accepted with a halal diet; audit signage, labels and dining halls for compliance with the halal dining program; assist SDHA staff in identifying religious dietary needs and products; assist in training staff members on halal dining, ingredients and accepted practices before, during and after Ramadan; assist chefs with tasting tables if needed; plan and implement dead week wellness food events for various religious dietary needs; help create marketing collateral for pertinent religious dining topics; engage on R&DE SDHA's social media pages; develop programming for halal diet related events; perform miscellaneous job-related duties as assigned.

postings.description: Stanford Libraries is seeking a collaborative, dynamic, and service-oriented Weekend Library Specialist to provide outstanding frontline customer services for the Library Circulation team at the Cecil H. Green Library. This position is 50% (20 hours per week), with a Friday-Sunday schedule. The Weekend Library Specialist is a member of the Circulation team and is primarily responsible for staffing public service desks, providing direct customer service for most of each shift, developing a broad understanding of library services, policies, resources and facilities and communicating that information to library users. The Specialist assists patrons with locating materials, navigating the library catalog and finding resources; answers library- and campus-related questions; processes routine circulation transactions such as checking materials in and out; and provides general support to library visitors. As backup to the Welcome Desk the Specialist assists with visitor registration and bag inspections. When assigned to the Media Center the Specialist supports patrons using media collections (microfilm, DVDs, video games) and related equipment. The Specialist makes referrals to supervisors and other library departments and engages Public Safety during emergencies or security-related incidents. In a backup capacity the Specialist also assists with behind-the-scenes library operations including picking requested books from the stacks, processing new materials, preparing returned items for circulation and supporting collection management projects such as shelf maintenance, record updates, shifting collections and shelving materials.
